reasons: plan.md's Proof section still does not list test_ratchets_eval_case_dot_rename_wins_over_a_surviving_sibling. This commit added the test's name only once, parenthetically inside the Risks section's second bullet ('... pinned by `test_ratchets_eval_case_dot_rename_wins_over_a_surviving_sibling`', line 124), but every other test this plan proves has its own dedicated Proof bullet ('tests/test_gate.py::<name> — <what it proves>'), including the closely related, pre-existing test_ratchets_drop_eval_case_dot_rename_fails (Proof, line 229) and test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop (Proof, line 237). The second review's third reason named 'plan.md's Proof/Order-of-work/Risks sections' together as the sections left stale; this commit closed Risks only. Proof is the section plan.md itself treats as the authoritative, exhaustive test-to-behavior mapping (its own interrogation answer 5: 'Every Proof item below names a test to be written... none claims an existing test already covers this behavior'), so a reader checking 'is panel decision #1's resolution actually pinned by a named test' via the Proof list alone will not find it there.

This is a real residual inconsistency, not a restatement of a deterministic check: plan_sync/content checks do not verify that every test function name mentioned in a docstring or Risks bullet also appears as its own Proof bullet, so nothing else will catch this gap before the owner reads the plan.
classification_reasons: check_ratchets runs at phases (c), (d) and (e) for every change type in every project the plugin drives (intent.md's own 'Affected users and systems'): wide blast radius for any drift between its documented semantics and its code.

The dot-rename-vs-survivor interaction is exactly the kind of fail-closed, security/correctness-relevant branch where the spec/plan/docstring's job is to keep a future maintainer from 'fixing' the deliberate asymmetry back into an evasion hole (panel decision #1's own stated risk) -- that job depends on the test being discoverable from the plan's canonical proof list, not just a parenthetical.

The spec itself is otherwise now tight on this point (Requirements and Design agree, checked independently) and the blast radius of this specific gap is a single missing cross-reference, which is why this is narrower than the second review's finding, not a reopening of panel decision #1.
attempted: Intent: the fix round's stated goal (close the documentation-consistency gap the second review found: spec.md Requirements, checks.py docstring, plan.md narrative) matches what this commit attempts; no scope creep, no reopening of panel decision #1's substantive outcome.

Spec and plan: read spec.md's Requirements bullet (around line 20-33) and its Design section (around line 125-140) side by side -- both now state the dot-prefixed-rename rule is evaluated independently of the survivor rule, citing panel decision #1; no remaining contradiction between the two sections (the exact gap the second review's first reason named is closed). Read plan.md's Risks section (the '--name-status -M diff cannot tell...' bullet) and confirmed it now cites the dot-rename sub-case and the pinning test by name. Read plan.md's Proof section in full and found the new test absent from it -- see reasons.

Proof: read plugin/gate/checks.py's dropped_eval_cases docstring as committed; it now states the dot-prefixed-rename rule is evaluated independently of the survivor check 'deliberately', citing panel decision #1 and explaining the rationale (a rename is itself how a case would be hidden) -- the exact gap the second review's second reason named is closed. Read tests/test_gate.py's new test_ratchets_eval_case_dot_rename_wins_over_a_surviving_sibling against the _ratchet_repo fixture: it dot-renames foo/a.yaml only, leaves foo/b.yaml untouched, and asserts the whole case 'evals/cases/foo/' is reported dropped -- a genuine pin of panel decision #1's chosen behavior, distinct from the pre-existing single-file 'bar' dot-rename test. Did not cite or rely on any evidence/claude-*.json, run-*.json or status.yaml gate record as proof for or against the diff.

Blast radius: this round's diff touches only spec.md, plan.md, plugin/gate/checks.py's docstring/comment text, and the test file; no guardrail files (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) are touched.

Policies: no security-baseline, data-conventions or coding-standards rule is implicated by prose/comment edits; the residual issue is documentation completeness relative to the plan's own stated convention, not a policy breach.

Tests: confirmed the new pinning test is not a tautology (it would fail under the originally-proposed 'filter dot_dropped against survivor_cases' fix the first reviewer wanted) and that no existing test was weakened, skipped or deleted this round.
